reach.problem: How many distinct people the money reached, and how often each of them saw it before the spend stopped buying new eyeballs.
reach.audience: A brand or media buyer deciding whether to widen the audience or cap frequency.
reach.followUps: Which placement is driving the frequency up? Is CPM rising with frequency, or independently of it?
reach.actions: Widen the audience, cap frequency, or move budget to the placements still reaching new people.

traffic.problem: How much of the traffic paid for actually arrives, and where the gap between a click and a landing view opens up.
traffic.audience: A performance buyer who owns click cost and is judged on qualified sessions, not clicks.
traffic.followUps: Which campaign loses the most between click and arrival? Is a dear click also a click that never lands?
traffic.actions: Scale what arrives, fix or pause what is paid for and never lands, and move budget off the dearest clicks.

video.problem: Whether the creative holds attention long enough to be worth the impressions, and where in the cut viewers leave.
video.audience: A creative lead choosing which cut to scale and which to re-edit.
video.followUps: Where does the drop happen — the hook, the middle, or the call to action? Does a longer watch actually convert?
video.actions: Scale the cuts that hold, re-edit the ones that lose viewers early, and stop the ones that lose them at the hook.

leads.problem: What a qualified lead actually costs once the forms that never open and the conversations that never reply are counted.
leads.audience: A demand-generation owner answerable for cost per lead and for what sales does with them.
leads.followUps: Which step loses the most — the open, the submit, or the first reply? Is a cheap lead also a lead that answers?
leads.actions: Scale the groups producing answered leads, rewrite the step that loses most, and cut the ones buying silence.

community.problem: What the account is buying beyond a click — followers, reactions and shares — and what each of those costs.
community.audience: A social or content lead whose target is an audience that stays, not a session that ends.
community.followUps: Which campaign earns engagement rather than only plays? What does a follower cost where it is cheapest?
community.actions: Scale what earns reactions, rework content that is watched and never acted on, and stop the rest.

app.problem: What an install costs by campaign, and whether the cheap installs are the ones that go on to do anything.
app.audience: A user-acquisition manager holding a CPI target and a budget to place against it.
app.followUps: Which campaign is under the CPI ceiling with volume behind it? Where does a cheap install stop being cheap?
app.actions: Scale under-target campaigns, optimize the ones close to the ceiling, and pause the ones past it.

sales.problem: What the spend returned — revenue, orders and ROAS — and which part of the path from click to payment is losing the money.
sales.audience: An e-commerce or performance owner judged on return, not on volume.
sales.followUps: Which campaign is under the ROAS floor? Where between the cart and the payment do the orders go?
sales.actions: Scale what returns, fix the step that leaks, and stop the campaigns under the ROAS floor.

risk.problem: Which campaigns crossed a line the account already set — frequency past its cap, cost per result deteriorating, spend with nothing to show — while the totals still looked acceptable.
risk.audience: A performance owner who needs to know what to stop today, before a weekly report turns it into a monthly loss.
risk.followUps: Which campaign crossed first, and is it one entity or the whole account? Did cost deteriorate because delivery collapsed, or because the audience stopped responding?
risk.actions: Pause what breached, rebuild the creatives that fatigued, and re-check the thresholds the board judged against.

traffic-landing-quadrant.problem: TikTok does not report a 0-100 traffic quality score, so this question cannot be answered from the data the platform returns. Ask it and the assistant will say which figure is missing rather than estimate one.
traffic-landing-quadrant.actions: No dashboard can be built for this one — a board needs a metric the platform actually reports. The closest served figures are landing page views, CPC and spend, which together show whether arriving traffic is worth what it cost.
traffic-landing-quadrant.followUps: Which served metrics come closest? Can landing page views against CPC answer the same question?

reach-frequency-daily.title: Reach & frequency daily report
reach-frequency-daily.prompt: My TikTok brand coverage has looked odd these past few days — check what actually happened over the last 7 days: are reach and average frequency better or worse than last week, is the money getting more expensive, and point out which campaigns have frequency high enough that I should cap it.

video-views-daily.title: Video views daily report
video-views-daily.prompt: Turn the last 7 days of my TikTok video-view campaigns into a daily report: four cards on top for video plays, 2-second plays, 6-second views and cost per 2-second view, each compared with the previous period; below them a line chart of daily plays and 2-second plays; beside it a pie chart of play share by placement, and say plainly if that split has no data source yet; then a wall of the top videos and a ranking of the ones with the most plays; and at the bottom a table per ad with plays, 2s, 6s, completions, completion rate, cost per 2-second view and spend, flagging completion rate below 5% in red.

video-completion-funnel.title: Play-through & completion funnel
video-completion-funnel.prompt: Show me at which second people swipe my videos away. Build a completion funnel: plays → 25% → 50% → 75% → completed, each stage showing the count and the share of plays — use plays as the denominator, not impressions. Put a completion-rate goal card on top with a 10% target. Next to it a bar chart comparing completion rate across content-length buckets. At the bottom a table listing both the "vs plays" and "vs previous stage" ratios for every milestone, and add 2s and 6s in for reference.

reach-cost-quadrant.title: Reach cost-efficiency positioning
reach-cost-quadrant.prompt: Build an efficiency positioning chart for my ad groups: X axis reach, Y axis CPM, bubble size spend, label the four quadrants "High efficiency high volume / High efficiency low volume / Low efficiency high volume / Low efficiency low volume", and flag bubbles with CPM above $4 in red. Add three cards on top: total spend, total reach, average CPM.

traffic-landing-daily.title: Traffic & landing daily report
traffic-landing-daily.hint: Clicks · CTR · CPC · Landing page views
traffic-landing-daily.prompt: Turn the last 7 days of my TikTok traffic campaigns into a live dashboard: four cards on top for clicks, CTR, cost per click and landing page views, each compared with the previous period; below them a daily line chart of clicks and landing page views. Then show me where the clicks were sent — a pie chart of click share by destination type and a table per destination with clicks, landing page views, arrival rate, CPC and spend — and say plainly if that breakdown has no data source yet. Finally the same question against what the data can answer: a ranking of the campaigns whose clicks actually arrive, and a table per campaign with clicks, landing page views, CTR, arrival rate, CPC and spend. Flag arrival rate below 50% in red.

traffic-hourly-monitor.title: Hourly traffic monitor
traffic-hourly-monitor.prompt: Open a real-time traffic monitor for today: a live status bar on top, then four cards for clicks, landing page views, landing rate and live CPC so far today. In the middle a two-hourly line chart of clicks and landing page views, next to it a ranking of the landing pages with the highest live landing rate. Then a row of three thumbnails for the creatives with the highest CTR, and at the bottom a table of the last six time slots, flagging abnormal load seconds in red.

traffic-landing-quadrant.title: Landing page efficiency positioning
traffic-landing-quadrant.prompt: Build me a landing page efficiency positioning chart: X axis the landing rate, Y axis a "traffic quality score" you work out for me — the kind that rolls landing rate, seconds on page and bounce rate into a 0–100 scale, bubble size is spend, label the four quadrants with what to do about each, and flag the ugly scores in red. Add three cards on top: total clicks, total landing views, overall landing rate. Beside it a ranking of the lowest landing rates, and at the bottom a table saying which quadrant each landing page falls in and the recommended action.

click-to-lpv-funnel.title: Click-to-landing drop-off funnel
click-to-lpv-funnel.prompt: I keep feeling that all my clicks leak away. Build a click-to-landing drop-off funnel: clicks → landing page views → stayed longer than 15 seconds → scrolled past half, each stage with count and conversion rate. Put a landing-rate goal card on top with a 75% target. Next to it a bar chart comparing landing rate across the four destination types, and at the bottom a table with landing rate, median load seconds and bounce rate per landing page, flagging landing rate below 55% or load above 3 seconds in red.

traffic-multisource-compare.title: Cross-source traffic comparison
traffic-multisource-compare.prompt: Add TikTok Ads clicks and Google Analytics sessions together into one big total-traffic card; then rank CPC with the highest CPC first, so I can tell which groups are buying the best-quality traffic. Below that a line chart overlaying TikTok, Meta and GA to compare the last 30 days, and finally a table with volume and cost per unit for each source.

cpl-volume-quadrant.title: CPL × lead volume positioning
cpl-volume-quadrant.prompt: CPL went up again this week and the money seems to be going to the wrong place — show me how I should adjust the budget. Ad group level, last 7 days.

instant-form-daily.title: Instant form leads daily report
instant-form-daily.prompt: A lead operations board for my TikTok Lead Generation campaigns using instant forms only — leave every other objective out — last 7 days, at ad group level. Four cards on top: spend, leads, cost per result and CTR against the previous period. Then a daily line of clicks and leads; leads by ad group; the ad-group table with spend, leads and cost per result; and a heatmap of leads by ad group and day. My goal this month is 1,500 leads.

form-submit-funnel.title: Form submission funnel diagnosis
form-submit-funnel.prompt: Lead cost suddenly got more expensive this week — show me where the problem is. My CPL target is under $3.00, mark whether I held it. The last 7 days of data is enough, I need to see down to ad group level, and flag the group that is unusually expensive.

dm-conversation-daily.title: TikTok messages daily report
dm-conversation-daily.prompt: Turn my TikTok message-objective campaigns into a daily report for the last 7 days: four cards on top for spend, conversations opened, cost per conversation and CTR, all compared with the previous period. In the middle a daily line for clicks and conversations opened. Below that rank the campaigns by cost per conversation, most expensive first, then a per-campaign table with spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC, conversations and cost per conversation. I would also like customer reply rate and first response time, if the source has them.

sales-app-daily.title: In-app purchase daily report
sales-app-daily.hint: Purchases · Purchase value · ROAS · Cost per purchase · last 7 days
sales-app-daily.prompt: Build a dashboard of in-app purchases for the last 7 days with five KPI cards for purchases, purchase value, ROAS, cost per purchase and spend, each compared with the previous period, two daily line charts of purchases and purchase value, a daily table and a table comparing campaigns.

web-sales-daily.title: Own-site sales daily report
web-sales-daily.hint: Spend · Revenue · ROAS · Purchases · this month
web-sales-daily.prompt: Show me a dashboard of this month's website ads: six KPI cards on top for spend, revenue, ROAS, purchases, CPA and conversion rate, each compared with the previous period; below them a daily line chart of spend and revenue trend; beside it a pie chart of revenue share per campaign; at the bottom a table per campaign with spend, impressions, clicks, purchases, revenue, ROAS and CPA, flagging campaigns whose ROAS is below 2 or whose CPA is above $22.

gmv-max-daily.title: GMV Max sales daily report
gmv-max-daily.prompt: Build a GMV Max sales report for the last 7 days. Show KPIs for spend, impressions, clicks, orders, GMV, ROAS, AOV and CTR, each compared with the previous period. Chart the daily trend of GMV, spend and ROAS; show GMV share by campaign and orders by ad group; surface the top selling creatives; and finish with a per-campaign table of spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, orders, GMV, AOV and ROAS, flagging the campaigns whose ROAS is below the account average.

checkout-funnel.title: Add-to-cart & checkout funnel diagnosis
checkout-funnel.hint: Funnel Add to cart → Checkout → Purchase
checkout-funnel.prompt: I want to know which stage the money leaks at. Build a checkout funnel dashboard: from landing page clicks, content views, add to cart, checkout initiated through to purchase completed, each stage showing people and the conversion rate "vs the previous stage" — do not use total clicks as the denominator for every stage. On top put add-to-cart count and checkout-initiated count, plus a goal gauge for a 40% checkout completion rate. On the right a bar chart comparing add-to-cart rate and checkout completion rate per ad group, and finally a table with the detail.

live-warroom.title: LIVE real-time war room
live-warroom.hint: Live now · Concurrent viewers · Peak viewers
live-warroom.prompt: I'm live right now — open me a LIVE war room: a red-dot LIVE status bar on top with the start time and how long I have been live; under it four cards for session viewers, current concurrent viewers, peak concurrent viewers and average watch time per viewer; in the middle a 5-minute concurrent-viewer line with new entrants per slot overlaid, next to it a traffic-source pie chart, and at the bottom a detail table per 5-minute slot, flagging any slot where concurrent viewers dropped more than 10% from the previous one, refreshing once a minute.

app-install-daily.title: Install acquisition daily report
app-install-daily.prompt: Show me a dashboard of this month's TikTok mobile-game install campaigns, one I can check daily: four cards on top for installs, CPI, clicks and spend, each compared with the previous period; below them a daily line chart of clicks and installs; beside it a pie chart of install share per campaign; and at the bottom a table of install detail per campaign with spend, impressions, CPM, clicks, CTR, CPC, installs, click-to-install rate and CPI, flagging CPI above $2.50 in red to remind me.

retargeting-daily.title: Retargeting daily report
retargeting-daily.prompt: Give me the last 14 days of my TikTok app retargeting: four cards on top for spend, results, cost per result and ROAS, each compared with the previous period; below them a daily line chart of spend and ROAS; a quadrant of results against ROAS per campaign; a ranking of the biggest-spending campaigns; a pie chart of spend share per campaign; and at the bottom a table per campaign with spend, revenue, results, cost per result and ROAS.

holdout-incrementality.title: Holdout incrementality analysis
holdout-incrementality.prompt: Retargeting ROAS is over four times and I don't quite believe it; we kept a 10% holdout control group. Build me an incrementality dashboard: four cards on top for direct ROAS, incremental ROAS, lift and organic-return share; in the middle a grouped bar chart comparing the conversion rate of the exposed group against the control group per audience; next to it an explainer card on how those two ROAS numbers differ; at the bottom a table with people exposed, people in control, control conversions, both conversion rates, the confidence interval and p-value of the lift, incremental orders and incremental ROAS — I want to know when incremental ROAS falls below 1.

skan-latency-monitor.title: SKAN postback delay monitor
skan-latency-monitor.prompt: Keep an eye on SKAN postbacks for me: a gauge showing postback completeness, two cards for events not yet returned and events masked by the privacy threshold, a pie chart of how the postback delay is distributed across hours, a table on the right listing each iOS ad group's currently reported figure, its estimated final figure and how far current ROAS is from the matured estimate, and finally a note reminding me not to conclude anything today. Also split SKAN postbacks by age group and gender, and list iOS ROAS per creative.

reach-quality-distribution.title: Frequency & reach quality distribution
reach-quality-distribution.prompt: Build me a "frequency health" dashboard: a funnel chart showing reach stepping down across the 1+ / 2+ / 3+ / 5+ tiers, next to it a bar chart comparing average frequency and CPM per ad group, a goal card on top with the target of keeping average frequency under 3, and at the bottom a ranking of the ad groups whose frequency has run too high.

reach-creative-wall.title: Placement & brand-coverage content wall
reach-creative-wall.prompt: Build me a content wall: a row of 6 vertical (9:16) content cards showing the 6 videos with the highest reach, each with a reach badge and the content name, below it a reach ranking per content, plus a "content freshness" table showing days live, frequency and the decay of each video, flagging decay above 30% in red.

video-engagement-quadrant.title: Watch-time × engagement quadrant
video-engagement-quadrant.prompt: I want to know which videos are worth more budget. Look at my recent video performance — how long people watch on average, whether they like, comment and share, which videos both hold attention and earn engagement, and which ones I should pull. Ask me which chart to use first, I'm not sure which shows it clearest.

video-hourly-monitor.title: Hourly video views monitor
video-hourly-monitor.prompt: Open a real-time video-views monitor for today: a live bar on top, then four cards for views, 2-second plays, 6-second plays and cost per 2-second play so far today. In the middle a two-hourly line chart of views and 2-second plays, next to it a goal card for 6-second views with today's target of 250k. Add a bar chart of completion rate by age group, and at the bottom a table of the last six time slots, flagging a clear drop in 2-second rate in red.

community-daily.title: Community interaction daily report
community-daily.prompt: Build me a community-interaction daily report for the last 7 days: four cards on top for followers gained, net follower growth, page views and cost per paid follower, all compared with last week. While you're at it, list the 2,862 accounts that unfollowed this week and the distribution of unfollow reasons — I want to know who left. The line chart in the middle overlays followers gained and net growth by day, so I can see at a glance how much unfollows ate. On the right a pie chart of the engagement mix — likes, comments, shares. At the bottom a table per campaign: optimization goal, followers gained, unfollows, net growth, cost per follower, page views, engagement rate and 7-day cohort retention.

community-efficiency-matrix.title: Engagement efficiency matrix
community-efficiency-matrix.prompt: Build me an efficiency matrix by ad group, only the follower-optimized groups (page-view optimization is off-scale and squashes the chart): X axis page views, Y axis cost per follower, bubble size spend, and label the four quadrants with whether to scale budget or turn off. Add three cards on top: total spend, page views, cost per paid follower. Next to it the five groups with the lowest cost per follower, and at the bottom a table of all nine groups with their quadrant and landing-page type.

instant-page-vs-web.title: Instant Page vs external site
instant-page-vs-web.hint: Instant Page vs Web · Load time · 7 days
instant-page-vs-web.prompt: Lately the external-site traffic looks off no matter how I slice it — check whether the page is too slow and eating my landing rate. How exactly do the in-app Instant Page and the external site differ, and by how much? Confirm with me which chart types to use first, I don't know what to look at — as long as the numbers reconcile.

gmv-roi-quadrant.title: ROAS quadrant diagnosis
gmv-roi-quadrant.prompt: Analyse TikTok Shop ad performance this month to decide which creatives and campaigns to scale, keep watching, optimise or stop. Show KPIs for spend, impressions, clicks, orders, GMV, ROAS, cost per conversion and CVR. Use a quadrant chart plotting spend against ROAS per creative, with bubble size showing GMV; rank campaigns by ROAS; show spend share by campaign; display a representative creative for each decision group; and provide a per-campaign table of spend, impressions, clicks, orders, cost per conversion, GMV and ROAS.

app-install-video-wall.title: Install-performance video wall
app-install-video-wall.hint: Video wall · Installs · CPI · D7 retention
app-install-video-wall.prompt: Build me an install video wall: the top 6 videos in a three-column grid, each thumbnail with an install-count and CPI badge; below it a bubble chart for positioning, X axis installs, Y axis D7 retention and bubble size spend, with the four quadrants labeled scale-budget or pull; on the right a ranking of cost per retained user. For the two iOS videos I want to treat the numbers as measured, ranked together with Android on CPI to decide budget up or down.

traffic-campaign-efficiency.title: Traffic efficiency by campaign
traffic-campaign-efficiency.prompt: Build me a TikTok Ads traffic efficiency dashboard for the last 7 days, from real data, broken down by campaign. If the source only returns per-ad rows, use ads and say plainly in the titles and the table which dimension you actually used. Show KPIs for clicks, landing page views (LPV), CTR, CPC and spend, compared with the previous 7 days where that data exists. Use a bar chart to compare clicks against LPV across campaigns, a ranking of the campaigns with high CPC or high spend but few LPV, and a detail table with campaign, clicks, LPV, CTR, CPC and spend. Finish with which to scale, keep watching, optimize or cut. If there is no breakdown at all, show the totals and say plainly which part is missing; do not invent figures.

traffic-ad-arrival-quality.title: Creative arrival quality, 30 days
traffic-ad-arrival-quality.hint: Ad grain · Arrival rate · Cost per landing view · 30 days
traffic-ad-arrival-quality.prompt: Build me a TikTok Ads creative arrival-quality dashboard for the last 30 days, from real data, broken down by ad. Only use figures TikTok Ads actually reports: impressions, clicks, landing page views, CTR, CPC and spend. Show KPIs for clicks, landing page views, arrival rate (landing page views divided by clicks) and cost per landing view, and state that the last two are computed from the figures beside them. Draw a funnel from impressions to clicks to landing page views so the two drop-offs are visible, a ranking of ads by arrival rate, and a detail table with ad, impressions, clicks, landing page views, CTR, arrival rate, CPC, cost per landing view and spend. Finish with which creatives to keep funding and which are buying clicks that never arrive. Do not use any web analytics, GA4 or Meta data, do not report dwell time, scroll depth or destination URL, and if a breakdown is missing show the totals and say which part is missing; do not invent figures.

community-engagement-ranking.title: Engagement ranking by campaign
community-engagement-ranking.prompt: Build me a dashboard ranking how much engagement my TikTok ads earned over the last 14 days, from real data, broken down by campaign. If the payload actually comes back per ad, use ads and say which dimension that is. Show totals for likes, comments, shares, video plays and spend; use a bar chart and a ranking to pick out where engagement is highest, where it costs a lot for little, and where there is room to scale. The detail table needs the campaign name, video plays, likes, comments, shares and spend. Do not require creative thumbnails. Finish with what to scale, what creative to rework and which tests to stop.

community-share-propagation-matrix.title: Community propagation matrix
community-share-propagation-matrix.prompt: Build me a TikTok Ads dashboard for how well traffic turns into sharing over the last 7 days, broken down by campaign; if the source only has per-ad rows, use ads and say which dimension that is. Show KPIs for page views, likes, comments, shares and spend. Use a bubble chart with page views on the X axis, shares on the Y axis and spend as the bubble size; split it into four groups at the medians: high traffic-high sharing, low traffic-high sharing, high traffic-low sharing and low traffic-low sharing. Add a detail table and a ranking of where the most shares came from. Finish with what to scale, keep testing, rework or cut. Do not infer reach, follower retention or organic figures the source does not provide.

app-install-efficiency-matrix.title: Install efficiency matrix
app-install-efficiency-matrix.prompt: Build me a TikTok Ads dashboard for app install efficiency over the last 14 days, from real data, broken down by campaign; if per-ad is the breakdown the source returns, use ads and say so. Show KPIs for installs, CPI, clicks and spend. Use a bubble chart with installs on the X axis, CPI on the Y axis and spend as the bubble size; lower CPI is better. Split it into four zones: many installs-low CPI, few installs-low CPI, many installs-high CPI and few installs-high CPI. Add a CPI ranking and a detail table with campaign, clicks, installs, CPI and spend. Finish with what to scale, keep testing, optimize or pause. Do not ask for an Android/iOS split, D7 retention or MMP data the current source does not provide.

risk-anomaly-overview.title: Risk & anomaly overview
risk-anomaly-overview.hint: Spend · CPM · CTR · Cost per result · 7 days
risk-anomaly-overview.prompt: Build me a risk review dashboard for my TikTok Ads account over the last 7 days, from real data, broken down by campaign — if the source only returns ad-level rows, use ads and say so. Show KPIs for spend, CPM, CTR, cost per result and results, each with its prior-period value and the change. Plot spend and cost per result as a daily trend line. Add a ranking and a detail table with campaign name, spend, CPM, CTR, cost per result and results, and clearly mark every row whose cost per result rose more than 20% against the prior period. Where there is no prior data, leave the cell blank rather than showing zero. Finish by naming which campaigns I should look at first and why.

risk-cost-efficiency-alert.title: Cost efficiency alert
risk-cost-efficiency-alert.hint: CPM · CPC · Cost per result · 14 days
risk-cost-efficiency-alert.prompt: Build me a cost efficiency alert dashboard for TikTok Ads over the last 14 days, from real data, broken down by campaign — use ads and say so if that is the dimension the source returns. Show KPIs for CPM, CPC, cost per result and spend with their prior-period values and changes. Use a bubble chart with results on the X axis, cost per result on the Y axis and spend as the bubble size, where a lower cost per result is better. Add a ranking by current cost per result and a detail table with campaign, spend, CPM, CPC, results and cost per result alongside its prior-period value and change. Clearly mark every row that deteriorated by more than 20% against the prior period, on the ranking, the bubble chart and the table alike. Do not assign a severity where prior data is missing. Finish by recommending whether to cut budget, optimise or pause.

risk-delivery-health.title: Delivery health
risk-delivery-health.prompt: Build me a TikTok Ads delivery health check for the last 7 days, from real data, broken down by campaign. Show KPIs for spend, impressions, results and conversions with their prior-period values and changes. The detail table needs campaign name, operation status and secondary status taken straight from the account data, alongside spend, impressions, results and conversions. Clearly mark campaigns that spent money but recorded no results at all, and campaigns with no impressions despite being enabled. Add a ranking of spend that produced no result. Use only the statuses the data source returns — never infer a status. Finish by naming which campaigns need their delivery checked first.

risk-creative-fatigue.title: Creative fatigue risk
risk-creative-fatigue.prompt: Analyse creative fatigue across my TikTok ads over the last 14 days, from real ad-level data. Show KPIs for frequency, CTR, spend and impressions with their prior-period values and changes. For each ad, give its frequency, how far CTR has fallen against the prior period, the status the data puts it in — new, watch, fatigued or healthy — and a recommendation that follows from that status; never invent a severity. Add a ranking by frequency, a strip of creative thumbnails, and a detail table with ad name, frequency, CTR, CTR change, spend, impressions, status and recommendation. Clearly mark ads whose frequency is past the threshold or whose CTR dropped sharply against the prior period. Finish by recommending whether to rotate the creative, leave it running or pause it.
